nodes.stableKey: Ledgerline billing service: codebase map › Usage and pricing § group#0

content.label: Usage and pricing
content.takeaway: Usage collection and pricing are handled by two functions, with one unconfirmed dependency.

nodes.stableKey: Ledgerline billing service: codebase map › Usage and pricing § text#0

content.markdown:
The code in `billing/usage/collect.ts` defines `collectUsage(accountId, period)`. It reads the `usage_events` table, selecting the account's rows whose `occurred_at` falls inside the period, and groups them by meter into usage lines. Events flagged `is_test` are skipped. It does not write to any table.

The code in `billing/pricing/priceUsage.ts` defines `priceUsage(lines, plan)`. It reads the `price_plans` table through a helper in the same file, `loadPlan(planId)`, and multiplies each line's quantity by the plan's unit price. Prices are held as integer cents throughout, never as floating-point amounts.

`priceUsage` probably also reads the `discounts` table. The file imports a helper called `discountFor`, and the name suggests a discount lookup, but I did not find a call site and have not confirmed that it ever runs. Treat this link as unconfirmed until someone traces it.

content.markdown: This section describes the two main functions for usage collection and pricing: `collectUsage` and `priceUsage`. It also highlights an unconfirmed dependency on the `discounts` table.

nodes.stableKey: Ledgerline billing service: codebase map › Tax § group#0

content.label: Tax
content.takeaway: Taxwell integration lacks defined retry and timeout handling, risking invoice generation.

nodes.stableKey: Ledgerline billing service: codebase map › Tax § text#0

content.markdown:
- The `TaxClient` class in `billing/tax/client.ts` has a `quote(draft)` method.
- This method sends the draft invoice to Taxwell, an external tax provider, via HTTPS.
- The request has an 8-second timeout, set on line 21.
- The API key is sourced from the `TAXWELL_API_KEY` environment variable during client construction.
- The response includes a tax amount per line, which `generateInvoice` incorporates into the draft before saving.

nodes.stableKey: Ledgerline billing service: codebase map › Tax § text#1

content.markdown:
- Retry mechanisms for the tax provider are undocumented.
- `TaxClient.quote` lacks retry code.
- It's unclear if callers retry, if the Taxwell client library retries, or what occurs if a quote times out.

nodes.title: Summary
nodes.stableKey: Ledgerline billing service: codebase map › Tax § text#2

content.markdown: The tax integration with Taxwell is implemented, but critical retry behavior and timeout handling are undefined, posing a risk to invoice generation.

nodes.stableKey: Ledgerline billing service: codebase map › Persistence and events § group#0

content.label: Persistence and events
content.takeaway: Invoice persistence is transactional, but event publishing has no retry mechanism.

nodes.stableKey: Ledgerline billing service: codebase map › Persistence and events § text#0

content.markdown:
- The code writes the finished invoice to two tables, `invoices` and `invoice_lines`, inside one database transaction in `billing/invoices/generate.ts`, lines 44–52.
- If either insert fails, the transaction rolls back and neither row is kept.
- The `invoices` row is written with the status `finalized`; I found no code path that writes any other status.

nodes.stableKey: Ledgerline billing service: codebase map › Persistence and events § text#1

content.markdown:
- After the transaction commits, `generateInvoice` calls `publishInvoiceFinalized(invoice)` in `billing/events/publish.ts`.
- That function publishes an `invoice.finalized` message to the `billing-events` topic.
- The payment and email services subscribe to that topic; I did not read their code.

nodes.stableKey: Ledgerline billing service: codebase map › Persistence and events § text#2

content.markdown:
- What happens when publishing fails after the commit is unknown.
- The code logs the error and returns, so an invoice can exist without its event, but I found no job that re-sends missed events and no note saying whether one is planned.

nodes.stableKey: Ledgerline billing service: codebase map › Interpretation § group#0

content.label: Interpretation
content.takeaway: `billing/pricing` is the pricing boundary, and `generateInvoice` orchestrates calls without its own logic.

nodes.stableKey: Ledgerline billing service: codebase map › Interpretation § text#0

content.markdown: My reading is that `billing/pricing` acts, in effect, as the pricing boundary: as far as I could see, no code outside it reads `price_plans`, so a pricing change should only need edits there. This is an interpretation of the current structure, not a rule the code enforces; nothing stops another module from querying `price_plans` directly.

nodes.stableKey: Ledgerline billing service: codebase map › Interpretation § text#1

content.markdown: In the same spirit, `generateInvoice` behaves like an orchestrator. It holds no pricing or tax logic of its own and only sequences the calls, which is why it reads so short for the work it starts.

nodes.title: Monthly run trigger
nodes.stableKey: Ledgerline billing service: codebase map › Open questions § text#0

content.markdown: - What starts the regular monthly run? The admin action is clear, but I could not find the scheduler that calls `generateInvoice` for every account.

nodes.title: Discount application
nodes.stableKey: Ledgerline billing service: codebase map › Open questions § text#1

content.markdown: - Does `priceUsage` really apply discounts? See the unconfirmed link above.

nodes.title: billing-events topic owner
nodes.stableKey: Ledgerline billing service: codebase map › Open questions § text#2

content.markdown: - Who owns the `billing-events` topic? No owner is listed in the repository.

nodes.title: Invoices table status column
nodes.stableKey: Ledgerline billing service: codebase map › Open questions § text#3

content.markdown: - Why does the `invoices` table have a status column if every row is written as `finalized`? It may be reserved for drafts, but nothing in the code says so.

nodes.stableKey: Ledgerline billing service: codebase map › About this map § text#0

content.markdown: This note maps the invoice path of the Ledgerline billing service as of commit `a41c9e2`. I read the code by hand; nothing here was generated by a tool. Every statement says how I know it: "the code does" means I read it in the file named, "my reading" is my own interpretation, "probably" means I suspect it but did not confirm it, and "unknown" means I looked and could not find out. Refunds, dunning and the customer portal are out of scope.
